headline: Sales and earnings climb on acquisitions and price increases
summary_short: Richelieu sales rose 12.6% y/y to C$562.0M (10.0% internal, 2.6% acquisitions) and diluted EPS rose 23.3% to C$0.53, including C$0.04 from a customs duty refund.
summary_long: Canada sales were C$300.2M (+10.2%) and U.S. sales US$186.7M (+12.9%). EBITDA rose 14.8% to C$65.5M, with the margin at 11.7% including about 60 bp from a C$3M refund of U.S. customs duties. Net cash was C$50.9M and working capital C$702.6M. Two acquisitions closed in the quarter (Solutions Acoustiques, Winnec) and Penrod, with about US$70M of annual sales, closed September 1. A C$0.1566 quarterly dividend was declared. No numeric guidance was given.
confidence_notes: Source is a newswire repost of the company's October 7, 2026 release (the official Canada NewsWire/SEDAR copy was not located). Figures were read via a page-summarizing fetch rather than the raw document. The shard EPS (C$0.53) matches the release. Reported operating cash flow was C$59.4M versus C$82.7M a year ago because of a working-capital build; the adjusted figure is shown in the KPIs.

drivers.explanation: 10.0% internal growth, mainly price increases to offset higher product and freight costs, plus 2.6% from acquisitions.
Growth in sales plus a C$3M customs duty refund booked as a reduction of cost of goods sold, worth about 60 basis points of margin.
Higher net earnings; the customs duty refund added C$0.04 per share.
Management framed the quarter as continued strong growth and strategic expansion, with five fiscal 2026 acquisitions adding about C$145M of annual sales.
